question: From first principles, how tall should letters on a road-facing business sign be, as a function of traffic speed, for a driver to notice, read, and act on it in time?
summary: Derived the same optical x kinematic mechanism and linear-in-speed functional form as USSC's speed/legibility-time tables (height in inches proportional to speed in mph); numeric constant ran ~1.9x too large because the stacked angular-degradation estimate (~20 arcmin) overshot the real effective driving-legibility threshold (~10-11 arcmin) implied by USSC data. Structure right, constant needed calibration data.
